gaia_target.notes: RUWE 0.98 (<1.4 single-star-like). AEN 0.16 mas with sig 39.8 is formally significant but typical of the G~12 calibration floor in DR3 (RUWE is the better binarity indicator at this brightness); ipd_frac_multi_peak=0 and ipd_gof_harmonic_amplitude=0.011 show no resolved-double signature; non_single_star=0, duplicated_source=False. RV -4.43 +/- 0.36 km/s from 25 transits; rv_amplitude_robust 5.5 km/s with rv_chisq_pvalue 0.23 (>0.01) -> no significant RV variability (Gaia RV epoch precision for an M0 at G_RVS~10.5 is a few km/s, so this only excludes large-K SB1s). Corrected BP/RP excess C*=0.004 (no blend). phot_variable_flag=VARIABLE: G std 6.0 mmag over 51 epochs (range 25 mmag) - consistent with spot modulation on an M dwarf. TIC v8.2 lists Gaia DR2 6355915466180482944 (DR2 id; DR3 id differs) and an epoch-2000 position.

nss.summary: No entries in any Gaia DR3 NSS table (two-body orbit, astrometric acceleration, non-linear spectro, VIM). Target is in vari_summary (in_vari_classification_result=True).

neighbours_note: All Gaia DR3 sources within 150" (57). dTmag relative to Stassun-estimated target T=11.097. depth_needed = depth*(1+f)/f with f=10^(-0.4 dT); assumes the full neighbour flux is in the aperture (upper bound on dilution, so a conservative mimic flag). Nearest Gaia source is 16.8" away; none within 16".

archival_summary.colour_note: Background stars are typically bluer than the M0 target (field median BP-T=1.12 vs target 1.80), so a given BP contrast corresponds to a ~0.68 mag larger T contrast. Same-colour value is the conservative case.
caveats: Photographic density is non-linear; injection adds background-subtracted real-star density stamps linearly. At the current position the plate density is only 1.6% of the target peak (near sky), so the plate is in its usable regime there.
Stamps are calibrated with Gaia BP (proxy for B_J); BP of G~19-20 stars is biased bright, which makes the limit conservative.
The limit applies within ~1 FWHM (3.4") of the 2026 position; Gaia DR3 independently shows no source within 16.8".
All later epochs (1992, 1995, 2000, 2014) have shift/FWHM < 1.5 and/or the current position inside the saturated halo, so they give no independent background constraint.

verdict.bound_companions: No Gaia evidence of a bound companion: RUWE 0.98, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, ipd_gof_harmonic_amplitude 0.011, non_single_star 0, no NSS solution, duplicated_source False, C* 0.004, RV scatter consistent with noise (rv_chisq_pvalue 0.23). This excludes companions that perturb the astrometry (roughly ~0.1-few arcsec, moderate contrast; RUWE<1.4 at 61 pc limits massive companions at ~1-10 au) but not close (<~0.1") faint or near-equal-period-blind configurations; high-resolution imaging (ExoFOP) and RV remain the tests for bound EBs. No co-moving Gaia source within 150" (the one similar-pm star at 95" has parallax 5.7 mas, not 16.2).
verdict.background_hidden_now: On the 1976.66 SERC-J plate the target sat 7.4" (2.2 x FWHM) from its 2026 position; the 2026 position is at sky level there and shows no source. Real field stars injected at that spot are recovered at >5 sigma down to BP=19.84 (dBP>=6.94; adopted 5-sigma dBP~7.25). In TESS band this excludes background stars with dT < ~6.9 (same colour as target, conservative) or dT < ~7.6 (typical bluer background colour). 1150 ppm needs dT<=7.4 (100% eclipse): a same-colour hidden star would need a >=69% eclipse - largely ruled out, fully ruled out for typical colours. 284 ppm needs dT<=8.9: background stars with dT~7.3-8.9 (needed eclipse 24-100%) are NOT excluded by archival imaging; a bright-enough hidden background star for 284 ppm is constrained only partially.
